defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: netrc_auth.py:17 expanduser prepends ~/ to NETRC value, absolute path never found
netrc_auth.py:12 empty NETRC string treated as valid, home dir parsed as netrc
test_netrc_auth.py:34 test only covers relative NETRC, misses absolute path case
votes.evidence_quote: `os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}")` unconditionally prepends `~/` to the `NETRC` value, so an absolute path like `/etc/netrc` becomes `~//etc/netrc` (e.g. `/Users/user//etc/netrc`).
votes.justification: The first finding names the expanduser call in get_netrc_auth as the cause. It says the call prepends ~/ to an absolute NETRC path, so the file is never found, which matches the known defect.
